standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded approximation lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Line 749: existence and uniqueness of the alpha-approximation f_alpha for every alpha, and again at line 761 for the coherence identity on overlaps.

core_obligations: Definition of sigma (proof lines 749-750): sigma(alpha) := f_succ(alpha)(alpha), reading off the successor approximation.

Five-line computation (lines 751-759): sigma(alpha) = f_succ(alpha)(alpha) = tau(f_succ(alpha) restricted to alpha) = tau of the displayed value set = tau of the same set computed through f_succ(beta) pointwise = tau(sigma restricted to alpha).
Coherence justification (line 761): the exchange f_succ(beta)(beta) = f_succ(alpha)(beta) for beta < alpha is exactly the agreement clause of the approximation lemma.
proof_roadmap: Pick the canonical successor approximation at each ordinal.
Evaluate the recursion equation at alpha.
Replace each approximation value by sigma's definition using coherence.
difficulty_reason: The general recursion theorem from the hierarchy of approximation functions (statement 744-749, proof 751-762): one definition plus a five-step display where the only nontrivial move, patching approximations on overlaps, is delegated to the cited uniqueness paragraph. H2: assembly over an established uniqueness lemma.
